$schema_note: Source of truth for agent work. Prose elsewhere is commentary; this file is authoritative. QA verifies THIS file, not chat history.

environment.$note: Pin every version a claim could depend on. QA verifies claims against THESE versions. Change any of them and you must bump pinned_on, which retires every claim verified under the old pin (PROTOCOL.md rule 3).
environment.pinned_on: <YYYY-MM-DD — bump whenever ANY version below changes>

depends_on: <claim ids this step relies on — these are what send it back to todo if refuted>

decisions.rationale: <why — cite claim ids, not vibes. These citations are what make the decision invalidatable.>
decisions.artifact: <file or path the decision produced, if any>

open_questions: <one unresolved question per entry, phrased so a yes/no or a number closes it>
$blocked_on_note: Ids of decisions or steps that cannot proceed. A failed QA verdict puts every decision citing the refuted claim in here (PROTOCOL.md rule 3).

claims.claim: <ONE atomic, checkable statement. Not 'X works with our setup' but 'X version N supports feature Y under condition Z.'>
claims.source: <URL of the official doc, or — for an empirical claim — what was measured>
claims.source_type: official_docs | release_notes | license_text | vendor_kb | code_inspection | direct_measurement | unverified_memory
claims.reproduction: <empirical and code_inspection claims ONLY: the exact command to re-run or file:line to re-read, the expected value, and the tolerance. Without this an empirical claim cannot be checked by anyone, including you in six months. Omit for documented claims.>
claims.confidence: unverified | verified | partially_supported | refuted | unreachable | stale
claims.verified_on: <YYYY-MM-DD the QA pass reached this claim, or null>
claims.verified_against: <the environment.pinned_on value it was checked under, or null>

claims.claim: EXAMPLE (delete): Flamenco 3.9.2 supports two-way path variables for cross-platform output paths.
EXAMPLE (delete): encoding a 300-frame 1080p sequence at the pinned settings peaks below 4 GB RSS.
claims.source: direct measurement on the pinned environment
claims.reproduction: /usr/bin/time -v ./encode.sh fixtures/300f_1080p -> 'Maximum resident set size' < 4194304 KB, tolerance +/- 10%

qa.note: Read this file and the artifacts it points at — never the chat transcript. Per claim: if method is 'documented', fetch the source and confirm it supports the statement FOR THE PINNED VERSION; if 'empirical' or source_type 'code_inspection', re-run the command in 'reproduction' and compare. RETURN one {id, pass, result, detail} per claim to the session agent that called you. DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE — it has one writer (PROTOCOL.md rule 4), and it is not you. The session agent appends your verdicts to qa.verifications and derives each claim's confidence from the latest one. Run as a subagent whose only input is this file.

verifications.id: <claim id — same spelling rule 4 uses in its {id, result, detail} handback>
verifications.result: CONFIRMED | PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED | DOES_NOT_SUPPORT | SOURCE_UNREACHABLE | REPRODUCED | NOT_REPRODUCED | NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_CHECKABLE | REFUTED | PIN_MOVED
verifications.detail: <what the source actually says, what the re-run produced, or how the refutation broke it>

resume_here: <ordered list: exactly what the next session should do first. MEMORY.md's Next section is prose for a human; this is the operative list.>
